title: K-Slide production plan
model_note: Requested for future implementation. This approval board does not change or verify the active model.
purpose: Choose the production implementation scope. Yes approves this item’s stated scope for follow-up work; No excludes it; Undecided is not approval. External items still need the named company prerequisites. No implementation starts from this board alone: tell Codex done when your review is ready.
reviewed_evidence: Current-main code and Notion production contract; 150 focused tests passed; two isolated defect probes reproduced. External production qualification has not been established.
effort_note: S / M / L are relative scope estimates, not delivery-time commitments.

groups.title: Scope & architecture
groups.description: Keep one product contract and make the approved work executable.

groups.title: Source & visual fidelity
groups.description: Everything visible has an honest, engine-owned representation.

groups.title: Meaning & verification
groups.description: Preserve the business decision, with traceable uncertainty.

groups.title: Employee experience
groups.description: A clear first answer, faithful detail, and useful recovery.

groups.title: VS Code & OpenCode
groups.description: Native host surfaces backed by the same engine.

groups.title: Backend & execution
groups.description: Durable, bounded, recoverable work with truthful completion.

groups.title: Security & privacy
groups.description: Company identity, confidential content, and isolation by construction.

groups.title: Runtime & operations
groups.description: A reproducible deployment that can be measured and supported.

groups.title: Quality & qualification
groups.description: Test the real employee path, including human understanding.

groups.title: Release & rollout
groups.description: Promote only proven candidates and recover safely from incidents.

groups.title: Optional improvements
groups.description: Useful extensions to decide separately from the production baseline.

items.title: Bind the work to the current repository and approved contract
items.outcome: Implement against the right code and a decision record you can audit.
scope: Refresh exact main before implementation; preserve local work
Map approved IDs to small changes, dependencies and validation
Record changes to scope instead of silently expanding it
acceptance: Every implementation change traces to an approved item
No approval is inferred from an undecided item
items.basis: Local checkout was 168 commits behind verified main at assessment time.

items.title: Preserve one engine and the evidence ownership boundary
items.outcome: Both hosts use the same trusted source facts, translation contract and completion rules.
scope: Keep /k-slide and one visible translation agent
Keep geometry, tables, numbers and coverage engine-owned
Keep source content untrusted and normal translation tools narrowly scoped
acceptance: Host-specific paths cannot bypass engine checks
Adversarial patches cannot redefine source evidence
items.basis: Production contract; implementation and qualification work proposed.

items.title: Version public contracts and compatibility rules
items.outcome: Schema changes and upgrades fail clearly instead of corrupting older runs.
scope: Maintain JSON/Python/TypeScript contract parity
Document compatible run, artifact and tool versions
Add explicit migrations only where needed
acceptance: Unsupported versions produce actionable errors
Approved migrations preserve evidence identity and historical artifacts
items.basis: Production contract; implementation and qualification work proposed.

items.title: Make complex backend boundaries easier to maintain
items.outcome: Reduce change risk around lifecycle, policy and certification without a rewrite.
scope: Refactor only measured coupling or duplication touched by approved work
Keep I/O adapters separate from domain decisions
Add focused typing and lint checks for changed boundaries
acceptance: Behavior remains covered by decisive regression tests
No abstraction is introduced without an actual caller or need
items.basis: Large lifecycle and certification modules warrant targeted maintainability work; no whole-codebase rewrite is proposed.

items.title: Define product readiness and accountable owners
items.outcome: Everyone can distinguish implemented code from demonstrated production readiness.
scope: Define release-blocking criteria and supported formats/topologies
Assign product, runtime, security and quality responsibilities
Record company prerequisites with explicit owners
acceptance: Readiness states are evidence-derived
Open external dependencies remain visible and cannot be marked complete by code tests
items.basis: Production contract; implementation and qualification work proposed.

items.title: Harden intake and immutable source snapshots
items.outcome: Only supported, authorized, unchanged inputs enter a run.
scope: Validate content signatures, archive relationships and path boundaries
Cover duplicate names, symlinks and source changes during intake
Preserve document-namespaced IDs and deterministic packet order
acceptance: Unsafe input is rejected before processing
Snapshots, hashes and IDs remain stable under retries
items.basis: Production contract; implementation and qualification work proposed.

items.title: Reconstruct raster and PDF tables as actual tables
items.outcome: Screenshots and PDFs retain rows, columns, headers, blank cells and units.
scope: Add engine-owned layout/table extraction for non-native inputs
Handle merged cells, footnotes and ambiguous boundaries
Route uncertain table structure to review before completion
acceptance: Equivalent PNG/PDF/PPTX tables preserve identical cardinality and meaning
Missing table structure cannot be accepted as ordinary paragraphs
items.basis: Reproduced: a visible 2×2 PNG table with four correctly recognized cells produced zero EvidenceIR tables and accepted an empty table patch.

items.title: Prove whole-page coverage beyond detected OCR text
items.outcome: Text or business structure missed by OCR cannot disappear from the coverage baseline.
scope: Compare layout/visual regions against native and OCR inventories
Track low-text, cropped, occluded and unexplained areas
Keep decorative classification policy-controlled
acceptance: Dropped text/callouts are caught by independent gold and coverage checks
Material unknown areas block DONE rather than shrinking the expected inventory
items.basis: Engine inventories are central to coverage; strengthen independent evidence that the inventory itself is complete.

items.title: Qualify Korean OCR and bounded recovery
items.outcome: Small, rotated, low-contrast and mixed-language content receives measured recovery.
scope: Pin local OCR models and configuration
Tune deterministic deskew, crop and scaling against representative artifacts
Retain competing candidates and stop after bounded recovery
acceptance: OCR assets work without network access
Unrecoverable text stays unresolved and is never completed from model familiarity
items.basis: Production contract; implementation and qualification work proposed.

items.title: Preserve PDF rendering and extraction fidelity

Reject or neutralize unsafe active/external content
acceptance: Crops point to the correct visible source locations
Golden PDFs preserve material footnotes and text order

items.title: Preserve PPTX shapes, tables, groups and render fidelity

Representative real PPTX files retain all business-relevant content

acceptance: False conflict resolution fails critical gates
A later file alone is not treated as authority

items.title: Deploy governed company terminology and mixed-language fidelity

items.title: Make faithful reconstruction readable and navigable
items.outcome: Users can move from the overview to complete document/page/table detail.

acceptance: Dense real business artifacts remain readable without omitted content

items.title: Build evidence drill-down and source comparison

items.title: Polish file selection and packet intake

items.title: Provide actionable errors and recovery messages

items.title: Harden the host-to-engine subprocess boundary
items.outcome: A blocked or crashed child cannot hang the employee session indefinitely.

Use safe structured transport instead of oversized payload command arguments

scope: Require an explicit approved engine binding for managed execution
Allow reference execution only behind explicit development mode
Tie semantic completion to the real finalizer and artifact checks
acceptance: The reproduced no-factory scoped-worker case fails closed
DONE requires valid TranslationPatch, canonical output and RUN_COMPLETE.md

items.title: Wire the durable worker to the real product pipeline
items.outcome: Heavy jobs execute the same engine, model path and verification as the employee command.
scope: Implement the approved WorkerEngine binding and company job-service adapter
Carry authorized run references and immutable environment identity
Use the same source/media/patch/finalizer path
acceptance: A real queued artifact reaches verified output through the managed worker
Reference adapters cannot qualify production transport or persistence
items.basis: Production contract; implementation and qualification work proposed.

items.title: Prove durable checkpoints and restart recovery
items.outcome: Completed work survives worker, browser and workspace loss.
scope: Commit state and outputs atomically at explicit stage boundaries
Reattach using persisted work queues and authorized run identity
Recover interrupted writes without accepting partial artifacts
acceptance: Kill/restart tests cover every material pipeline boundary
Recovery neither loses committed work nor fabricates completion

items.title: Separate safe retries from semantic repair

acceptance: Load tests preserve per-scope ordering and isolation
No two workers can commit conflicting results for one operation

items.title: Make cancellation and timeouts terminate actual work

acceptance: Cancellation works before claim, during inference and during finalization
